_doc: GAMEPLAY-DRIVER-2 self-test + the reference day/night A/B.
Frames the player lance, spawns a MECH and a VEHICLE side by side under
identical light, then captures the SAME pose at noon and at midnight so a
rendering change can be judged under both light conditions (the day AND
night verdict rule) without hunting for a mission that ships as night.
Every claim is asserted against world state read back through the channel,
not against ack text -- see the assert_* steps.
_camera_note: Use MC2_CAMERA_PARK, not the `camera` verb, to pin an A/B pose.
`camera <x> <y>` calls eye->setPosition(pos, TRUE) -- the SWOOPY goal-seek --
and the in-mission scripted camera keeps writing the pose afterwards, so the
two arms end up framing different scenes. Measured with the verb: the arms
landed on different terrain and one even had the HUD faded in, making the
luminance comparison meaningless. camera_park does a one-shot HARD set
(setPosition(p, FALSE)) plus freezeScriptedCameraForCapture(), so every arm
shares one frozen pose. This is the standard mc2_10 baseline pose.

steps._note: wait past the camera_park frame so both arms share the frozen pose
